name: Right Aortic Arch

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Imaging-based diagnostic criteria for right aortic arch

criteria.description: Demonstration of aortic arch coursing to the right side of the trachea on imaging studies (CT, MRI, or echocardiography)
Identification of vascular ring formation causing tracheoesophageal compression
Presence of associated congenital heart defects such as tetralogy of Fallot or aberrant subclavian artery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of right aortic arch is required; assessment for vascular ring and associated cardiac anomalies supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities; clinical symptoms vary depending on presence of vascular ring or associated defects

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right-sided aortic arch visualized on imaging

pathognomonic.notes: May cause airway or esophageal symptoms

common.notes: Common in cases with vascular ring
searchTerms: swallowing problems due to esophageal compression

common.symptomName: Stridor or wheezing from airway compression
Cyanosis in presence of associated cardiac defects
common.notes: Seen when congenital heart disease coexists

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to vascular anomalies

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure
failure to gain weight as expected

occasional.notes: May be related to arrhythmias in associated defects

rare.notes: Uncommon, may be related to arrhythmias

rare.symptomName: Chylothorax due to thoracic duct compression
searchTerms: fluid around lungs from lymph leak
chest fluid due to duct compression

imaging: Chest X-ray showing right-sided aortic arch
CT angiography or MRI confirming right aortic arch and vascular ring
genetic: Genetic testing may identify syndromic associations

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of two aortic arches forming a complete vascular ring
More severe airway and esophageal compression symptoms
Right subclavian artery arising aberrantly from left-sided aortic arch
Usually no right-sided aortic arch on imaging

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress or stridor in infancy
Cyanosis or signs of congenital heart disease
references: Morrison JL, et al. Right aortic arch: clinical features and imaging findings. Radiographics. 2018.
Mullassery D, et al. Vascular rings and slings. Paediatr Respir Rev. 2017.
